en.greeting: Hi! Today we're going online: social media, phone and laptop problems, and the news. Many of these words look like Indonesian, but they're used a little differently in English, so let's go step by step.

steps.title: Social media words
steps.text: You already know email, app, password and log in. Let's add social media.
steps.body:
Many of these words are both a **thing** (noun) and an **action** (verb): *a post / to post*, *a like / to like*, *a comment / to comment*.

Two small traps: you **comment on** something (*She commented on my post*: Indonesian *komen fotoku* has no word for **on**). And the people who follow you are your **followers**.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Rina posts a photo of her new café on Instagram.

question.prompt: Dimas writes 'Congratulations!' under Rina's new photo. What did he do?
question.explanation: Writing something under a post is a comment: **comment on** her photo (don't forget **on**). You follow a **person**, not a photo, and Rina posted the photo, not Dimas.

steps.title: Going viral, going live
steps.text: Now the words for things that get very popular online.
steps.body:
In Indonesian we say *sangat viral*. In English, viral is something that **happens**: a video **goes viral** (past: **went viral**). So not `is very viral`. Before a noun it's fine: *a viral video*.

*Siaran langsung* is **go live**: *I'm going to go live at 8.* Careful: **live** alone means *tinggal*, so `I'll live on TikTok` means you'll move into TikTok!

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Bu Ani's small batik shop has just posted its first video on TikTok.

question.prompt: Complete: If this video ___ viral, the shop will get a lot of new customers.
question.explanation: The chunk is **go viral**, and after *if* about the future we use the present: **goes** viral. `is very viral` copies Indonesian *sangat viral*, and *make* doesn't go with viral.

steps.title: Your phone: charger, battery, signal
steps.text: First, a surprise: in English, HP is a computer brand!
steps.body:
Say **phone**, **mobile** (British) or **cell phone** (American), not *HP*. *Handphone* is used in Singapore and Malaysia, but most English speakers don't say it.

The **charger** is the thing (alat cas); **charge** is the action (ngecas). The battery is **low**, then it **runs out** (habis). British people also say *my battery is flat*, Americans *my battery is dead*; informally, *my phone died*.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Budi didn't answer Sari's messages all afternoon. Now he replies.

question.prompt: Complete: Sorry I didn't reply. My phone battery ___ on the KRL.
question.explanation: A battery **runs out** (past: **ran out**) = *baterainya habis*. `finished` and `was over` are word-by-word translations of *habis*: English doesn't use them for batteries.

steps.title: Problems and fixes
steps.text: Now, what to say when something goes wrong, and how to fix it.
steps.body:
In Indonesian *error* is like a describing word (*laptopnya error*). In English **error** is a **thing** (noun), like a message on the screen. So not `My laptop is error`: say **My laptop isn't working** or **It shows an error**.

An app **crashes** (closes suddenly); a screen **freezes** (past: **froze**, *nge-hang*). Fixes: **restart**, **update**, **back up** (action, two words) / *a backup* (thing), like *log in / login*.

examples.en: My printer isn't working. Can you help me?
examples.id: Printer saya error. Bisa bantu saya?

examples.en: I get an error message when I open the banking app.
examples.id: Muncul pesan error waktu saya buka aplikasi bank.

examples.en: The game froze, so I restarted my laptop.
examples.id: Gamenya nge-hang, jadi saya nyalakan ulang laptop saya.

examples.en: You should update the app. The old version crashes a lot.
examples.id: Sebaiknya kamu perbarui aplikasinya. Versi lamanya sering tiba-tiba tertutup.

examples.en: I back up my work files every Friday.
examples.id: Saya mencadangkan file kerja saya setiap Jumat.

steps.title: Build the sentence
steps.text: Sari is calling the IT department at her office. Help her describe the problem.

question.prompt: Arrange the words: HP saya menampilkan pesan error.
question.solution: My phone shows an error message.
question.explanation: **error** is a thing, so it needs a verb before it (**shows**) and **an** (error starts with a vowel sound). *error message* = pesan error. And *HP* in English is **phone**.

steps.title: The news
steps.text: Last group: words for following the news.
steps.body:
**news** ends in -s, but it's **not plural**: it's **uncountable** (we don't count it one by one, like *water*). So **the news is** (not `are`), **good news**, never `a news`. **Fake news** (hoaks, berita palsu) is the same. *Hoaks* is **a hoax** in English, but *fake news* is more common.

Give a source with **according to** (menurut): *according to Kompas*. For your own opinion, say **In my opinion**, not `according to me`.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Sari's aunt shares a message in the family WhatsApp group: 'Hot water cures dengue!' It isn't true, and there's no source.

question.prompt: Complete Sari's reply: ___ Please check before you share.
question.explanation: News is uncountable, and so is **fake news**: no *a*. `It's a fake news` is the classic mistake. Breaking news is real news that is happening now, so it doesn't fit.

steps.text: Here's the whole lesson on one page.

I'm going to go live at 8.

I read the headlines every morning.
According to Kompas, fuel prices are going up.
tips: Not `very viral`, `is error` or `a news`: the video **went viral**, my laptop **isn't working**, I have **good news**.
**news** looks plural but is singular: **the news is**. Same for **fake news**: *That's fake news.*
In English, say **phone** (or mobile / cell phone), not *HP*. **go live**, not *live* (live = tinggal).

id.greeting: Hai! Hari ini kita online: media sosial, masalah HP dan laptop, dan berita. Banyak kata di sini mirip bahasa Indonesia, tapi dipakai sedikit berbeda dalam bahasa Inggris, jadi kita jalan pelan-pelan, ya.

steps.title: Kosakata media sosial
steps.text: Kamu sudah tahu email, app, password dan log in. Sekarang kita tambah media sosial.
steps.body:
Banyak kata ini bisa jadi **benda** (kata benda) sekaligus **tindakan** (kata kerja): *a post / to post*, *a like / to like*, *a comment / to comment*.

Dua jebakan kecil: kamu **comment on** sesuatu (*She commented on my post*: *komen fotoku* dalam bahasa Indonesia tidak punya kata untuk **on**). Dan orang yang mengikutimu adalah **followers**-mu (pengikut).

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Rina mengunggah foto kafe barunya di Instagram.

question.prompt: Dimas menulis 'Congratulations!' di bawah foto baru Rina. Apa yang dia lakukan?
question.explanation: Menulis sesuatu di bawah postingan itu komentar: **comment on** her photo (jangan lupa **on**). Yang di-follow itu **orang**, bukan foto, dan yang mengunggah foto itu Rina, bukan Dimas.

steps.title: Jadi viral, siaran langsung
steps.text: Sekarang kata-kata untuk hal yang jadi sangat populer di internet.
steps.body:
Dalam bahasa Indonesia kita bilang *sangat viral*. Dalam bahasa Inggris, viral adalah sesuatu yang **terjadi**: sebuah video **goes viral** (lampau: **went viral**). Jadi bukan `is very viral`. Sebelum kata benda boleh: *a viral video*.

*Siaran langsung* itu **go live**: *I'm going to go live at 8.* Hati-hati: **live** saja artinya *tinggal*, jadi `I'll live on TikTok` artinya kamu mau pindah tinggal di TikTok!

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Toko batik kecil Bu Ani baru saja mengunggah video pertamanya di TikTok.

question.prompt: Lengkapi: If this video ___ viral, the shop will get a lot of new customers.
question.explanation: Paketnya **go viral**, dan setelah *if* tentang masa depan kita pakai bentuk present: **goes** viral. `is very viral` meniru *sangat viral*, dan *make* tidak dipakai dengan viral.

steps.title: HP-mu: charger, baterai, sinyal
steps.text: Pertama, satu kejutan: dalam bahasa Inggris, HP itu merek komputer!
steps.body:
Bilang **phone**, **mobile** (British) atau **cell phone** (Amerika), bukan *HP*. *Handphone* dipakai di Singapura dan Malaysia, tapi kebanyakan penutur bahasa Inggris tidak memakainya.

**Charger** adalah bendanya (alat cas); **charge** adalah tindakannya (ngecas). Baterainya **low** (lemah), lalu **runs out** (habis). Orang Inggris juga bilang *my battery is flat*, orang Amerika *my battery is dead*; dalam obrolan santai, *my phone died*.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Budi tidak membalas pesan Sari sepanjang sore. Sekarang dia membalas.

question.prompt: Lengkapi: Sorry I didn't reply. My phone battery ___ on the KRL.
question.explanation: Baterai itu **runs out** (lampau: **ran out**) = *baterainya habis*. `finished` dan `was over` adalah terjemahan kata per kata dari *habis*: bahasa Inggris tidak memakainya untuk baterai.

steps.title: Masalah dan solusinya
steps.text: Sekarang, apa yang diucapkan kalau ada yang tidak beres, dan cara memperbaikinya.
steps.body:
Dalam bahasa Indonesia *error* seperti kata sifat (*laptopnya error*). Dalam bahasa Inggris **error** adalah **benda** (kata benda), misalnya pesan di layar. Jadi bukan `My laptop is error`: bilang **My laptop isn't working** atau **It shows an error**.

Aplikasi **crashes** (tiba-tiba tertutup); layar **freezes** (lampau: **froze**, *nge-hang*). Solusinya: **restart**, **update**, **back up** (tindakan, dua kata) / *a backup* (benda), seperti *log in / login*.

examples.en: My printer isn't working. Can you help me?
examples.id: Printer saya error. Bisa bantu saya?

examples.en: I get an error message when I open the banking app.
examples.id: Muncul pesan error waktu saya buka aplikasi bank.

examples.en: The game froze, so I restarted my laptop.
examples.id: Gamenya nge-hang, jadi saya nyalakan ulang laptop saya.

examples.en: You should update the app. The old version crashes a lot.
examples.id: Sebaiknya kamu perbarui aplikasinya. Versi lamanya sering tiba-tiba tertutup.

examples.en: I back up my work files every Friday.
examples.id: Saya mencadangkan file kerja saya setiap Jumat.

steps.title: Susun kalimatnya
steps.text: Sari menelepon bagian IT di kantornya. Bantu dia menjelaskan masalahnya.

question.prompt: Susun kata-katanya: HP saya menampilkan pesan error.
question.solution: My phone shows an error message.
question.explanation: **error** adalah benda, jadi butuh kata kerja di depannya (**shows**) dan **an** (error diawali bunyi vokal). *error message* = pesan error. Dan *HP* dalam bahasa Inggris adalah **phone**.

steps.title: Berita
steps.text: Kelompok terakhir: kata-kata untuk mengikuti berita.
steps.body:
**news** berakhiran -s, tapi **bukan jamak**: kata ini **uncountable** (tidak dihitung satu per satu, seperti *water*). Jadi **the news is** (bukan `are`), **good news**, tidak pernah `a news`. **Fake news** (hoaks, berita palsu) juga begitu. *Hoaks* dalam bahasa Inggris adalah **a hoax**, tapi *fake news* lebih sering dipakai.

Sebut sumbernya dengan **according to** (menurut): *according to Kompas*. Untuk pendapatmu sendiri, bilang **In my opinion**, bukan `according to me`.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Tante Sari membagikan pesan di grup WhatsApp keluarga: 'Hot water cures dengue!' Itu tidak benar, dan tidak ada sumbernya.

question.prompt: Lengkapi balasan Sari: ___ Please check before you share.
question.explanation: News tidak bisa dihitung, begitu juga **fake news**: tanpa *a*. `It's a fake news` adalah kesalahan klasik. Breaking news adalah berita sungguhan yang sedang terjadi, jadi tidak cocok.
